subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose flow now, and what trigger plus local editor/tempfile safety contract should it use?
rationale: The missing capability is clear from source, but launching an environment-selected local editor and writing prompt drafts to disk crosses a process and sensitive-content boundary that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
options.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, visible errors, tests, and docs.

options.title: Hold For Contract
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers choose the permanent trigger and document local editor and tempfile rules.

options.title: Decline Editor Handoff
options.body: Prefer inline multiline editing or composer expansion instead, then close or narrow this request by maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Core Flow
recommendation.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, visible errors, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the most detailed prior review and have the strongest history across the TUI runtime, command, docs, and editor surfaces involved.
